en: (no.- 1202 gha) (Title- Ḍākinīkalpaḥ) (Extent- 14 leaves)
(Subject:
Tantra) Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa. [Now, the seven defects of the *vāra* are written:
Ātāretā(-)pāvetā-yoginī-dṛṣṭottaradiśā-jalanikaṭa-jājanī-daśadi.

The afflictions of nose ailments, toothache, hemorrhoids, scabies, leprosy and other such diseases, as well as suffering in the hands, feet, and so forth— [the remedy for] these is the worship of a virgin (kumārī) on a Monday. If fever occurs, [one should perform this] during the two periods of evening and morning at the garden (vāṭikā).

Having entered the middle of the Ghaṭavī forest, there occurred the wandering of many bhūtas, piśācas, and other spirits, resulting in abdominal pain, fever, and suffering in the hands, feet, and other limbs. On a Tuesday, for the sake of pleasing a vetāla among eleven men, an animal sacrifice was offered; consequently, the patient suffered from fever and abdominal pain.

Having eaten at some gathering, he arrived at the time of the leftovers; right there he was seized by fear—pain in the bones, pain in the belly, and a great terror for seven days, or perhaps for a month.
For that purpose, [he prepared] rice, food, oil, and beans, along with oil and molasses.
Having wandered here and there and distributed whatever was to be given at a certain divine shrine,
he was seized by a fever on a Wednesday; he arrived in the midst of a cremation ground where two beings were present—
one a Mleccha and the other a Brahmin— and [he suffered from] pain in his feet and toothache.

For ten days, one should carry either a white cloth or a black cloth for the sake of this religious duty; by doing so, a hundredfold merit is produced. On a Thursday, a fever arises in the stomach. At the time of twilight, he went to the foot of a tall tree; there, O Brahmins, his vision became non-existent.

Having established a fire near the water for washing, a bath was performed; this is his vision. (7) O Brahmins, at that very place, during the hour of midday, a black animal must be offered as a sacrifice by a group of nine men. For twenty days, there will be doubt even after that. (7) On a Friday, a fever shall arise.
They went somewhere from the village into the middle of a forest; there, on the way, they came upon a temple. Suddenly, right there, a sound arose from a beast-offering intended for Śani.
On Saturday, one is seized by a fever; [this occurs] on the path in the middle of a forest, in a cremation ground.

If one becomes afflicted near water, or if abdominal colic occurs at the root of a tree near a body of water on the seventh day of the bright fortnight, or the second day of the dark fortnight, an offering of a black animal should be made; black beans (*māṣa*) should be given, and it will become auspicious. This is the treatment for fever. Now, the treatment for fever according to the lunar days (*tithi*): [fever on] the first day (*pratipad*).

One should diligently cause [the patient] to take *royasabrahmaṇī*, *ḍākinī*, *nīla*, *guggulu*, *sikhipitta*, as well as *gośṛṅga* combined with *sarṣapa*. All the limbs will be consumed, food will not be taken, and a severe fever will arise; moreover, a headache will be produced for him.

When there is a fault due to the wrong lunar day (apratipad), one should offer bali-oblations in the eastern direction consisting of milk-rice (pāyasa) and rice mixed with sesame (kṛśara), along with cakes (apūpa) and other such items. I shall now declare the mantra for the fault caused by a ḍākinī: Oṃ, obeisance to the Brāhmaṇī who has emerged from the Veda and who causes the three worlds to take their seats!

HĀNA (2) MĀRAYA (2) BALIṂHUṂPHAṬ (2) SVĀHĀ (2). (1) I shall now describe the second [rite]: the Ḍākinī Karmukārī makes one tremble, shiver, and indeed utter delirious speech. I shall explain the *bali* offering for her, by which happiness is attained: it should consist of cakes (*apūpikā*).
I shall likewise proclaim the mantra for the month of Māgha, by which happiness is attained:
Oṃ namaḥ vārāharūpadhāriṇi kaṭa 2 caṭa 2 chidi 2 bhindi 2 daṃṣṭreṇa saṭakaṃ kira 2 mahākrodhaṃ bhava vikaṭe huṃ phaṭ svāhā.

Alas! (2) On the third [day], I shall speak; listen, O child, as I tell you. Alas! For one who possesses the signs of the fierce Raudrī, terrible anger, the breaking of the limbs due to fever, and pain in the feet—of such a person, I shall describe the strength [of the affliction] and likewise the seven-fold food.

Furthermore, one should give that entire heart-lotus through the meditation on the center at a crossroads. Here I shall proclaim the mantra by which happiness is attained: *Oṃ namaḥ bhagavate cāmuṇḍe rudrakrodhasvare rudrakrodhavināśinī asurapramathanī*.

*Ca-kī* (2), *ḍi-kiri* (2), *khaṭa* (2), *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. The *bilva* oblation at the foot of a tree (3). On the fourth lunar day (*tithi*), I shall describe the one who acts as a hide-worker for the *ḍākinīs*. She has the form of a comet (*ketu*). From her arise lice, nits, and the like; there is pustules, iron-like sores, fever, and violent trembling.

I shall now describe the signs of such a person and the *bali* offering for him: one should provide cooked food accompanied by ghee, liquor, and meat; one should offer incense and ghee, and likewise cause clarified butter (*samarpitā*) to be given.
Herein I shall proclaim the mantra by which happiness is attained: *Oṃ namo bhagavatyai jvā...*

*linī* (2) *huṃphaṭ* (4) *pṛcchīṃ* (2) *huṃ* (2) *phaṭsvāhā* (4). On the fifth [day], I shall describe the *tanumāvīca-ḍākinī*: she causes pain in the sides, pain in the heart, and likewise pain in the head; furthermore, while eating, there occurs a single swelling on the cheek.
One should likewise cause an offering (*bali*) with these very characteristics to be presented: liquor, *kṛśira*, and red perfumes. Here I shall proclaim the mantra by which happiness is attained:
Oṃ namo bhagavati kumāri-hana (2) svara (2) khakha-mara (2) māra (2) hā.

*Raya (2) juṃjuṃ phaṭ svāhā (5). I shall now describe the sixth [deity], the Ḍākinī of terrible form. I shall declare the offering for her whose characteristics are such: rice, meat, clarified butter, and cilika, combined in equal parts. Having gone toward the southern direction at midday, one should present the bali-offering.*

One who knows the ritual acts, being free from transformation, should offer liquor, meat, and the sacrificial oblation (*bali*). *Oṃ namaḥ mahāvāyave namaḥ pañcāyai | Oṃ namaḥ bahulāyai namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* (6) Now I shall describe the practice for the seventh [day], concerning the *Cāṇḍālī* and the *Ḍākinī*.

A crow, as well as the sky and a house on the throat [of the victim], appear; I shall now describe the *bali* offering for one who possesses such signs. One should offer goat meat, wine, and *cilakālopi* in the western direction at the time of twilight when it is empty. Oṃ.

Homage to the Blessed Caṇḍālī, O moon-faced one! Hana (2), kaṃpa (2), kaṃpaya (2), dhuna (2), halohale svāhā! (7) On the eighth day, I shall describe the Ḍākinī Kumbhakārī; she causes trembling, she causes terror, and indeed a terrible fainting fit occurs. Such is the characteristic of him [who possesses it].

I shall tell you the ritual: one should offer goat meat and a heart-lotus wrapped in a red cloth as a *bali* offering at the crossroads at midday while alone. When the asterisms Anurādhā, Maghā, Mūla, Bharanī, Punarvasu, Puṣya, or Revatī are present, our disease will perish.

Oṃ namo bhagavati brahmarave vara naṭa naṭa caṇḍānane hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. On the ninth [day], I shall describe the Ḍākinī who is a Kṣatriya woman: burning fever and phlegm arise, and the eyes become blood-red; for one who has these characteristics of Indraśaṃ, I shall here prescribe the bali offering.

Chili-cakes, fruits, and three kinds of pastries, as well as cooked fish-meat and various flowers— one should offer this bali at the time of twilight, resorting to the northern direction. *Oṃ namo bhagavati kṣatriṇi hūṃ kāmeśvari akṣa...*

*Mālādhare phaṭ svāhā*. (1) On the tenth day, I shall fully describe *Saucakī* and *Ḍākinī*, who possess fierce forms, are great Durgās, and are overwhelmed by infinite fear. A violent fever arises, and one becomes like Śiva with a flickering lamp. These are the forms of the Yakṣas belonging to him.

I shall offer here an oblation (*bali*) consisting of *bharbharas*, cooked rice, fish, and likewise *vaṭikās*, combined with liquor and meat, along with a lamp fed by sesame oil. Having taken recourse to the western direction at the time of twilight, one should present the oblation with the mantra: *Oṃ sara mantra prasphura mahāsvāda dha*.

*riṇidamaḥ* (2) *huṃ phaṭ svāhā* (10). On the eleventh day, I shall declare the well-known *sūpakāriṇī*, as well as fever (*jvara*), colic (*śūla*), and the great terror of burning (*daha*). I shall describe the offerings (*bali*) for one who possesses these signs: seven types of food and seven kinds of grain.

At the time of twilight, one should offer a bali-oblation mixed with blood, meat, and the like, along with ghee and jaggery, while facing the south-eastern direction; by that, happiness is attained. *Oṃ namo bhagavate vibhave viṣṇo gate bhajaṃ nirvarṇatāve śeṣu ci agninilaye uccheṣṭe*.
O you whose complexion moves like the wheel of Viṣṇu’s disc! On the twelfth day, Āḍakinī indeed becomes Viṣṇu-tā-baludhāriṇī;
his fever arises, and his complexion becomes pale like the sky.
Having observed such a sign, I shall here declare the bali offering for him: various cooked foods and diverse kinds of nourishment.
One should offer an oblation (*bali*) of fish, meat, and likewise all kinds of food; one should also prepare perfumes and other offerings.

One should cause perfumes, flowers, and incense to be presented in the western direction. At the time of twilight, one should offer the oblation at a crossroads according to the prescribed rule: *Oṃ namo bhagavati pracaṇḍe ruṃ hūṃ phaṭ*.

Svāhā! (12) Now hear this great form of Ḍākinī for the thirteenth day: the forehead becomes distorted and bilious; likewise, diarrhea, colic, and headache arise. I shall now describe the bali offering for one who possesses these characteristics of Indra-śaṅka: [mada...]
One should offer a bali-oblation toward the south consisting of meat, rice, and various sweet foods;
from that, happiness is attained. Oṃ namaḥ mahābhairavāyai hana (2) maraja (2) ka ṭa (2) kara (2) mahākaṭa (2) nikara-mahākaṭa-mahābala hūṃ phaṭ.

Svāhā! On the fourteenth day, the Cārmakārī (leather-worker woman) appears in a form of wrath, possessing great strength. She constantly carries anger, and one should indeed seize her with a firm grasp. One should likewise offer raw meat, fish, flesh, and so forth, seven times. Having first resorted to the tenth lunar mansion, one should offer the bali-oblation at midday. Oṃ Na.
O Bhagavatī, O beloved of the neck, O you of fierce power, O terrible one with a face of wrath, svāhā!
(14) On the fifteenth day, she is seized by the Yoginī; of this there is no doubt. Side-pain, heart-pain, and abdominal pain arise; he in whom these signs appear is [seized].

I shall eat strength-providing foods such as cakes, fried pastries, and sweets combined with sugar, as well as very pure curd-rice mixed with kulattha beans and fish, accompanied by grapes and the like, along with perfumes, flowers, and so forth;
whether on a riverbank or in a cremation ground, provided it is accompanied by perfumes, flowers, and the like. Indeed, [this is] most excellent.

One should resort to the *sīmā* and offer a *bali* at the time of twilight; by that, happiness is attained. Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One, Siddhi-yoginī, Caṇḍe (2), Pracaṇḍe, Pracaṇḍānane (2), Hana (2), Māraya (2), give here what is desired, svāhā! (15). [Thus ends the Tithi-Ḍākinī-kalpa.]

In Aśvinī, there is no fault from the falling of shadows, miscarriage, or childbirth; however, there may be pain in the ears, nose, and throat, as well as an aggravation of Vāta and Pitta. In Āśleṣā, there is distress in the middle of the body due to fat;
when it is released, an offering (bali) should be made toward the fifteenth direction (South). In Hasta, one touches again... [the beginning].

One should worship that Aryaman at a crossroads and perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*). Under the asterisms of Punarvasu, Rohiṇī, Hasta, Svāti, Śravaṇa, and Śatabhiṣaj, one should give oneself as a gift, offer milk-food to a Brāhmaṇa, and offer oblations into the fire. [Then] Bharaṇī.

When there is the defect of *cabhūta*, there is pain in the head, all the limbs, and horripilation, and the teeth chatter; death occurs in the seventh month from the onset of the illness. Having made a cake (*piṣṭa*) in the shape of a ram and offered it with five types of grain at a crossroads, a sacrifice to the spirits (*bhūtayāga*) must be performed, and the worship of a young girl (*kumārī*) should be conducted in the house.

In the house of a person afflicted by *vyaṅga*, one should perform the funeral offering (*śmaśānabali*), place eight lamps, and give sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*). One should perform the gift-giving and the conquest of the house. [The asterisms are] Bharaṇī (1), Kṛttikā (11), Rohiṇī (14), and Mṛgaśirā (17). One should give gifts of black objects and red cloth, and offer the nails into the fire. (2) Oṃ! In the case of Kṛttikā, there is suffering from new vehicles.

One should offer oblations of *thikā* flowers mixed with ghee. (1|8|15|14) One should perform the gift of ghee and sugar, the gift of yellow cloth, the feeding of Brahmins, and the *tiḥ-homa*. (3) Oṃ! In Rohiṇī, there is a violent fever; [the patient] sees red garments and blood, and breathes heavily. To him, one should give *palāyaṃ*.
One flees from suffering; there arises a loathsome, foul-smelling, and harsh secretion of phlegm.
Having made a bull out of flour and placed it in a vessel filled with food, one should worship it and offer it along with unctuous water, incense, and lamps.
One should offer an oblation of raw rice (*āmabali*) to the deity Tvaṣṭṛ; a bath for liberation from disease [is prescribed] under Citrā;

and under Anurādhā, one should perform the third *mṛta* (rite for the deceased). The tongue speaks incessantly, the heart melts, and the back and the interior of the chest feel as if they are being split; there is great pain in the heart and intense thirst.
(71|3|5|8) Having made a paste of ground meat, one should place it in a vessel along with food, wine, and sweets, and offer it as a *dṛṣṭi-bali* oblation accompanied by incense and lamps. Dvi-...
On the third day, at a crossroads, one should perform worship of the *bhūta-maṇḍala*, worship of the *stūpa*, and the bath for liberation from disease.

Under the asterisms of Hasta, Anurādhā, Mūla, Ārdrā, Śatabhiṣaj, Kṛttikā, Svāti, Mṛgaśirā, and Śravaṇa, there is suffering at the end of the month; [remedies include] bitter flowers, fragrant substances, incense, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*).

Having worshipped Soma with nine [offerings], one should offer curds and milk. (5) [Mṛ] (30|18|) (12|18|). One should perform the gift of silver-rice and the gift of white milk, and conduct the fire-oblation in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
(5) Oṃ Ārdrā, Skanda, Vikuru, Cakṣus, Tāva, Vaktrā, Pāṇḍuvarṇa, Vepas, Surā, Rātrau.

One should remain awake during the day and sleep at night. Having made a man and a woman out of flour and placed them in a vessel containing food, sesame seeds, and milk, one should offer an oblation (*bali*) at a solitary tree, recite the mantra of the deity of sacrifice, perform worship of the *liṅga* with milk-rice (*pāyasa*), and give a cow as a gift until one is satisfied.
In the constellation Ārdrā, one should worship Śambhu with offerings of *dhatura* flowers, incense, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*), reciting "Obeisance to Saṃbhava" three times;
then one should offer oblations of honey, ghee, and sugar-candy [in the number] 11,
7, 28, and 17, give a gift of white cloth, give a gift of yellow cloth, and perform a honey-oblation (*madhu-homa*) under Punarvasu.
One suffers from the flow of saliva and tears, tremors, heavy calves, and a lack of appetite for food.

(45 | 21 | 18 | 28) Having fashioned the form of a woman or a man out of black-gram flour (*māṣapiṣṭa*) and worshipped it, one should offer a timely oblation (*bali*) consisting of cooked rice, wine, sweetmeats (*modaka*), fish, and pus.
One should worship Maheśvara and perform the propitiatory rite (śānti) for Sunday; one should offer a bali-oblation at a crossroads.

On the Punarvasu day, for seven nights, one should worship Aditi with jasmine flowers, sandalwood paste, incense, and offerings of molasses and rice, and should offer oblations of ghee and rice. Tṛ...
In the *Tiyemate* [sections] (7|51|8|28), one should perform the offering of yellow garments and the flower-homa.

Oṃ! With flowers, the arms and hands are placed upon the chest; the tongue and teeth chew; these two feet are cool. (7|7|20|21). [The offerings include] *puṭaka*, sesame, rice, liquor, meat, and so forth.

Having placed a *kaṃ* lotus leaf [as a vessel], there is an offering (*bali*) in the cremation ground, a bath, and [offerings] in the hand and the ear. According to another opinion, there is a seven-day period for flowers. Therein, with offerings of *mānavaka* flowers, *khadira* incense, and sweetmeat cakes (*khaṇḍavartaka*), Bṛhaspati is invested with the sacred thread; thus, having fully worshipped Bṛhaspati, [one offers] milk and clarified butter.
"One should offer *khaṇḍa* (sugar-candy)" means one should perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*) with food, water, and flowers. Under Āśleṣā, one lives by means of death and fortune;
there is a disease arising from the provocation of wind and phlegm, or suffering from wind and bile, and colic pain; in the first month, it affects the region of the three joints (*trika*).
(35) Having seen his debt as three parts, and having fashioned a vessel made of clay for death, he should worship Maheśvara together with Gaṇeśa—
[the deity] who has seven faces, three heads, and eight feet— with offerings including the seven grains, food, liquor, and meat at a crossroads.

One should offer water and perform the worship of Nairṛtī, Vāruṇī, and Rākṣasī; there is also the worship of Mṛṣāntikakumārī and the bath for liberation from disease. Under Anurādhā, Maghā, Bharaṇī, and Punarvasu, according to another opinion, death occurs; [one should worship] with offerings of Agastya flowers, ghee, molasses, and incense.
Having worshipped the serpents with the mantra "stusarpebhyaḥ," one should offer oblations from the vessels for the serpents in eight ways.
One should perform the ritual bath at a sacred ford (tīrtha-snāna) and the nail-homa (nakha-homa). (1) Oṃ: Under Maghā, the heart is pierced;
there is fever, anger, disease, burning of the head, pain in the heart, and the affliction of a ḍākinī. Mu...

One should know that pacification (*śānti*) arises when [the affliction] occurs in the middle of eating. Having fashioned an extremely formidable lion out of flour (*piṣṭa*), along with wine, *abhimodaka* sweets, and the five grains,
one should place it in a vessel and give it to a twice-born (*dvija*) for the sake of pacifying the calamity on the second day.
One should mutter the *bhūtatṛpti* hymn, the *tvāḍapakṣa*, and the *kapala*; [perform] the bath for liberation from disease; [offerings] on the day of Śatabhiṣaj;
[recite] the *drāyāṃśata* and the *bhiṣaji-reka-nyāṃ*; on the Maghā asterism (20), [use] jaggery and guggulu incense;
on the third [lunar day] (20|27|18|33), [there is] the gift of all types of clothing, with offerings of ghee-filled cakes (*ghṛtapūra*). U-dī.

Having worshipped *Ritā* and *Itipitṛt-kṣam*, one should offer oblations of ghee, sesame seeds, and rice; one should perform the fruit-homa by giving cow-hide and gifts. (10) *Oṃ*, in the constellation Pūrvā-phālgunī, there is a defect in my heart, and a defect in the eyes caused by blood; furthermore, there is the defect of a *ḍākinī* located in the bladder, [caused by] *alaṃktu-kuṭāṇḍa*.

If there is intense fever, burning pain, or death on the fifth or twelfth day, one should perform the eightfold rite with *māka* curd and food; according to another opinion, death occurs on the previous [day].
There, having worshipped Bhagavat Bhaḍāṃsa with *karavīra* flowers, incense, lamps, and offerings, [one should offer] a *māṣa*...

One should offer oblations with *ktā* and *vyava*; [the nakṣatras] Puṣya (11), 17, 28, and 17; the giving of one's own color, the giving of *saga*, the feeding of Brahmins, and the performance of a *gandha-homa*.
Under Uttarā-phalgunī, there is a severe fever; in the house or temple, having made a red figure of fear, one should conquer the tongue.

One should offer a heart-shaped *piṣṭa* (flour) cake, fashioned in three forms, filling another vessel with it, and present the *bali* offering to Miśāla; one should perform the *skandayajña* and sacrifice a tawny cow (*kapilā*). For liberation from disease, one should perform a ritual bath under the asterisms of Śravaṇa, Rohiṇī, Puṣya, Punarvasu, and Śravaṇa, and perform a pacification (*śānti*) rite. [The rest follows.]

In the *Maitra-uttarā* [nakṣatra], for ten nights, one should worship Aryaman with offerings of red lotus flowers, guggulu incense, clarified butter, and milk; having worshipped him, one should offer oblations of barley-meal (*saktu*) and *trivṛt* (*triyaṅgu*). One should perform the gift of a cow (*godāna*), other gifts, and the honey-oblation (*madhu-homa*). (12)

Oṃ! Hand-borne, red-colored, afflicted by disease, excessively delirious, having diarrhea, with a heart that breaks and eyes that are bound—this is the fault of Saptakṣetra during the arrival of the Moon. One should offer incense made from *vaṃśa* (bamboo) and *piṣṭa* (flour), perform rites for women, and offer a sacrifice (*bali*) at a crossroads or at a tree.

One should give [the gift] within three days; according to another opinion, up to the end of a fortnight. There, having worshipped the Sun with offerings of *kavīramalaka* incense and flowers while reciting "ruṭatyamiti," one should offer curd (*dadhi*).
(15|33|15|21) One should perform the gift of curd, the gift of a cow, and the *siṭu* oblation.

(13) Oṃ. In the constellation Citrā, during the conjunction with the Moon, there occurs a reddish disease. For three months, there is pain in the sides, movement [of the limbs], vomiting, and deafness; or there is affliction in the neck and long-sightedness. This is the fault of a ḍākinī. Having assumed the form of a piśāca, it afflicts one. One should worship it with perfumes and flowers. When the six-fold food is prepared, [offer] liquor and meat.

One should cause a child to be given to a nurse. Under the asterism Citrā, for eleven days, one should worship Tvaṣṭṛ with offerings of *japā* flowers, *padmaka* incense, and sweetmeats (*modaka*), and perform an oblation of "variegated rice" (*citrānna*).
[The nakṣatras] Citrā (11, 21, 18, 21). There is the gift of raw food and water.

One should perform the gift of a vessel full of cow-products and offer molasses into the fire with the mantra: "Oṃ svāti! Terrible disease, phlegm-born fever, and pain in the hips [occur]; this affliction lasts for ten days at the place of heroes (vīrasthāna). There is a fall on the fourth day. Having fashioned an animal out of bean-flour and prepared five kinds of food, one should perform the rite at a crossroads.
If a dog is seen falling on the ground, scratching its limbs, or howling, one should offer a *bali* sacrifice there.
Having made a flour-image of a ram (*piṣṭameṣa*) and filled a basket (*puṭraka*) with twenty-one cakes along with liquor and meat, one should carry the *bali* at night. One [should do this].

One should perform the *bhūtayāga* at this tree with offerings of water and flowers; thereafter, there is liberation from the *śāti* [obstacle]. One should bathe in the *aśvinī*, *puṣya*, *anurādhā*, or *svāti* [nakṣatras] to avoid death. [The results for] the ten [nakṣatras] are:
*nakra* (Capricorn), flower, rice-porridge, *ṣaṣṭhī*, rice, silver, and rice-grains. (11|5|28|17) [The results for] the *svāti* [nakṣatra] are: silver and rice-grains.
Having worshipped Vāyu with offerings, saying "Vāyo, vāya," one should worship Vāyu and offer barley (*yava*).
One should offer black cloth and molasses, and offer *vīhaṇa*. (15) Oṃ!
Under Viśākhā, there is a crooked discharge, and pain in the eyes, phlegm, teeth, tongue, and so forth, as well as constriction and ear-ache.

One should offer a bali-oblation with the form of this [deity] resounded by the sound of musical instruments; one should declare the eight limbs (aṣṭāṅga) and worship the directions with seven types of grain, sesame seeds, walnuts, barley, māsa-beans, and milk-rice (pāyasa).
Rudra is pleased; at night, one should give the gift of a cow and offer a bali-oblation at a crossroads after bathing.
In Viśākhā, for one full night, one should perform the offering of black *tulasī* flowers, *devadāru* wood, incense, molasses, and food offerings;
on the third [lunar day] (15|18|28|11), one should offer white substances, deer fat, and ghee as oblations. 16. Oṃ, in Anurādhā, [there is a mark] in the anus and the penis. Viṃda.
The *tripiṭaka* disease causes a burning sensation in the eyes and throughout the limbs; it is caused by the affliction of spirits (*bhūtadoṣa*).
One should perform a spirit-sacrifice (*bhūtayāga*) for seven days or for a fortnight, and on the seventh day, one should perform it at the house [of the afflicted].
One should have [the patient] drink ghee and worship the Sun and other deities, as well as the god Vaiśravaṇa, and offer funeral cakes (*piṇḍa*) to the ancestors.
One should offer the gift of food along with the vessel to Kubera; thereafter, one should bathe.
[Then] one should perform the gift of a cow (*godāna*), offer the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), and recite: *oṃ namo astu sarpebhyo ye ke ca pṛthivyām adhi ye antarikṣe ye divi tebhyo sarpebhyaḥ*.

Homage to those serpents who dwell in the woods, who frequent the forests, who sport in the thickets; homage to those serpents who dwell far away in the sky, who are in the rays of the sun, and who have made their abodes in the waters. (17) Om, to the eldest... in the finger...

The burning of the Pitakas shall cease; during the appearance of the moon, for two fortnights in the middle and three fortnights at the end, there will be danger to the Pathaka. Having fashioned an elephant out of flour, one should construct a water-wheel (ghaṭīyantra) and place it at a crossroads;
having filled it with food offerings, one should offer the bali at night.
One should offer a sacrifice of a single bull and worship one's chosen deity with offerings of meat, fish, and rice.

Then, one should cause Śambhu to be worshipped. On the third lunar day of the month of Jyeṣṭha (11|5|37|17), one should give gifts of sesame oil and jaggery, and offer oblations of water (18). Oṃ, on the Mūla nakṣatra, there is the gift of a woman.

The six defects of the gods are: burning of the head and feet, diarrhea caused by the wind-phlegm (vāta-śleṣma) humor, dryness of the throat, trembling, and the appearance of the moon; the period of the three [days] at the end of the fortnight is also a period [of defect]. One should fill the pitcher with five, three, or two [measures]; a herd of horses should be kept at night.
Having gone to a cremation ground, one should worship one's chosen deity. One should perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*) with ghee, rice, and barley;

offer a sacrifice to the Mothers (*mātṛkā-yajana*) and give a bali-offering to the spirits (*bhūta-bali*). For those who have been freed from disease, one should bathe under the asterism Rohiṇī and give gifts.
[The mantra: *tṛmū* (1|11|1|1). One should give a gift of black gram (*māṣa*) and a tawny cow (*kapilā-gau*).

One should offer oblations with *naṃpātakeśara*. (1) Under *Pūrvāṣāḍhā*, there is the affliction of vomiting (*chardi*), fever (*svāsa*), and *sannipāta* [disorder]; one snorts from the nose, suffers from foul-smelling root-pains in the limbs, and has the affliction of *cakradoṣa*.
One should worship the Sun, fill a water-jar (*kuṃbha*), and worship the goddess Caṇḍakā in the fire of the sacrificial ground.

One should recite the *rākṣasī* mantra for Mahādeva: *snānaṃ re aci mū tṛ*. (15|| 7|| 1||) (8||) One should offer gifts of pearls, oil, and molasses, and perform oblations with curd (*dadhi*). (20) Oṃ! Under the constellation Uttarāṣāḍhā, there is fear of shadows, headache, and the Makara [sign] may arise; one should give offerings of rice mixed with sesame seeds.
One should offer a sacrifice on the path as an oblation for the gaze of people; perform worship of Mahādeva accompanied by the eight classes of spirits (*bhūta-aṣṭaka*);

one should perform the pacification of the planets (*graha-śānti*) with sixteen kinds of food, including meat, rice, sweetmeats (*modaka*), and cakes (*apūpaka*), and satisfy the twice-born (*dvija*);
one should also satisfy the Goddess; the satisfaction of the young girls (*kumārī-tarpaṇa*) is for the worship of the *khecarīs*; these are the defects and the sacrificial offering (*bali*).
One should perform the Godāna rite and offer honey into the fire. Oṃ. In Śravaṇa, there is the affliction of spirits; first, seventh, and middle [periods] (10), and the end (11).
There is indeed the Vaiṣṇavī desire-disease, skin disease, wind-disorder, pain in the sides, dysentery, the onset of fever, and pain in the head.
One should worship with milk-rice, liquor, meat, and sesame seeds; one should offer four oblations (*bali*).
Under *Dhaniṣṭhā* (11|36|14|21), it causes agitation of the chest and family affliction.
There is a burning sensation at first for twenty days, and in the middle of two months, there is a form like a crocodile filled with water.

One should fill a jar with milk, cooked rice, and a cloth pouch containing camphor; having first performed the single-portion offering (*ekāki-bali*), one should examine it at dawn and determine the directional division. If [the signs] appear in the east, there will be health;
if in the south, one should predict death; if in the west, there will be a state of stagnation; and if in the north, [prosperity].
In the house of one born under Śatabhiṣā, another deity may enter the family deity;
[therefore,] for the sake of pacifying the nine houses, one should offer oblations of *śānti*-oil, jaggery, and *lodhra* powder.
(23) Oṃ! Under Śatabhiṣā, there is an excess of phlegm, bodily pain, and the body trembles after every meal.
On the sixteenth lunar day under the asterism of Śravaṇā, one should offer milk-rice mixed with sesame seeds and perform a libation of eight handfuls of water.
On the second day, one should worship Kumārī and feed five Brahmins. One should fill a vessel with rice mixed with meat and sesame cakes, and offer a lamp on the riverbank at dawn.

One should offer a living being as a sacrifice, worship Varuṇa and Viṣṇu; then his disease shall cease and his fortune shall increase. (18 || 27 || 18 || 20 ||) One should give the gift of a bull, perform various kinds of giving, and offer honey into the fire. Under the asterism Pūrvābhādrapadā, [one should worship] Brahmā.

There is a fault [if this occurs] during the arrival of the moon; for eighteen days in the middle and twenty-eight days at the end, one should perform five *kuṃbha* rites. One should bring a black animal to the cremation ground (*śmāna*) and offer four oblations (*bali*). There, one should worship the *puṭka* and a cauldron (*kaḍāha*) filled with oil.
Having prepared a vessel made of iron, one should cook [the substance] for one *ghaṭikā* and cast what has been produced [into it].

Furthermore, by bathing under the asterisms of Aśvinī, Maghā, or Citrā, no disease shall arise. One should offer oblations of sesame, ghee, and sandalwood; likewise, one should offer a forehead mark (*tilaka*) and gold. (25) (20.2.27) [The same applies to] the offering of a *tilaka* and gold.

Oṃ. When foot-pain occurs under Uttarābhādrapadā, one is released from the path either within a fortnight or after twenty-eight days; there is no harm from the fault of the fortnight or the path. [U] (15) (13||18|| 12|).
It has been stated that the gift of clothing [should be made]. Oṃ. Under Revatī, there is severe fever and blood [disorders].
The *Netra* [Tantra] describes the symptoms of the most terrible fever (*mahāghora-jvara*) as follows: it lasts for thirteen days;

at the end of the eighth day, the patient is released; there is pain in the sixteen parts of the body, shivering, a sensation of being crushed, and a distaste for food and milk; sesame seeds and flowers should be offered upon the head.

Under the asterisms of Vivāha, Aśvinī, Puṣya, Hasta, Anurādhā, and Viśākhā, one should perform an auspicious ritual bath; it shall be beneficial. [The numbers 19, 18, 20, and 24. One should give gifts of silver and rice, give a horse, and offer the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*). May there be auspiciousness for the birth-asterism and the birth.

The year obtained from the *rāśyāṭya* [method] should be increased by one and placed in three positions. These are to be multiplied respectively by 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 8, and then divided [by those same numbers]. If the results obtained are zero at both the beginning and the end, there will undoubtedly be suffering in that year.

"If the middle [channel] is empty, there is Indra; if the three are empty, there is indeed death. This result—the day of death—should be declared from the *trināḍīcakra*. Thus ends the verse. Now, O Gaurī, listen; I shall explain the characteristics of the *mṛtyucakra*, beginning with Ārdrā.

O Supreme Goddess, when the Sun and Moon enter the Khetrināḍī in a single asterism, three [periods] will occur; in that nāḍī, death will certainly take place. When Śauri (Saturn) and Bhauma (Mars) are in the nāḍī, there will be suffering from fever. [Likewise for] Jīva (Jupiter), Śukra (Venus), and Budha (Mercury).
From that, happiness arises for him.
